title: The Sunday Read: ‘Who Is the Bad Art Friend?’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: In early January, I got an email out of the blue from a writer named Dawn Dorland, who I'd never met before and didn't know.
sentences.zh: 一月初，我突然收到了一封来自一位名叫道恩·多兰的作家的邮件，我以前从未见过她，也不认识她。

sentences.en: The email said that she was involved in a dispute with another writer named Sonia Larson and that she felt she'd been plagiarized.
sentences.zh: 邮件里说她和另一位名叫索尼娅·拉尔森的作家之间发生了纠纷，她觉得自己的作品被抄袭了。

sentences.en: She thought it might be a topic that I might want to explore.
sentences.zh: 她认为这可能是一个我感兴趣的话题。

sentences.en: I have to say that to be approached this way from somebody who's in the middle of a dispute is not exactly unusual for me because I write a lot about tangled disputes.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，以这种方式被身处纠纷中的当事人找上门，对我来说并不算罕见，因为我经常撰写关于复杂纠纷的报道。

sentences.en: On the other hand, it's possible that I was the 17th door that Dawn knocked on.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，也有可能我是道恩敲开的第17扇门。

sentences.en: My name is Robert Kolker and I'm the writer of Who is the Bad Art Friend, which appeared recently in the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫罗伯特·科尔克，是《谁是糟糕的艺术朋友》一文的作者，该文最近发表在《纽约时报杂志》上。

sentences.en: Without giving away too much of the story, one side of the dispute felt that an aspect of her life was sort of being kidnapped by someone else and put into someone else's fiction.
sentences.zh: 在不剧透太多故事细节的情况下，纠纷的一方觉得她生活中的某个侧面被别人“绑架”并写进了别人的小说里。

sentences.en: But on the other side,
sentences.zh: 但在另一方看来，

sentences.en: the other writer felt harassed that the first writer was being irrational and was set out to destroy her for what she thought was something that artists do all the time.
sentences.zh: 那位作家感到被骚扰了，她认为第一位作家很不理智，一心想毁掉她，而她所做的一切，在她看来不过是艺术家们常做的事。

sentences.en: And what interested me the most was that the disagreement between the two writers was something that started out very small
sentences.zh: 最让我感兴趣的是，这两位作家之间的分歧起初非常小，

sentences.en: and then got bigger and bigger very gradually until it finally landed in federal court in a defamation and copyright infringement case
sentences.zh: 然后逐渐演变，最终闹到了联邦法院，成了一起诽谤和版权侵权诉讼，

sentences.en: where the two people involved could really easily be affected for the rest of their lives by this disagreement.
sentences.zh: 而这场分歧可能会轻易地影响到当事双方的余生。

sentences.en: I had to ask myself, how did it get this bad?
sentences.zh: 我不得不问自己，事情怎么会变得这么糟糕？

sentences.en: Where did it go wrong?
sentences.zh: 到底是哪里出了问题？

sentences.en: What happened moment by moment to cause this escalation?
sentences.zh: 究竟发生了什么，导致了事态一步步升级？

sentences.en: I haven't really wanted to weigh in on Twitter, but there is one thing going around that is worth correcting.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不想在推特上发表意见，但有一件事正在流传，值得澄清一下。

sentences.en: After this story was published, there were rumors going around that Dawn Dorland actually pitched the New York Times to write about herself,
sentences.zh: 在这篇报道发表后，有传言称道恩·多兰实际上是主动向《纽约时报》投稿，要求报道她自己，

sentences.en: which is to suggest by implication that she was somehow orchestrating the coverage.
sentences.zh: 这暗示她是这场报道的幕后操纵者。

sentences.en: And that could not be further from the truth.
sentences.zh: 而事实远非如此。

sentences.en: I had made it clear to Dawn from the beginning what my intentions were, which was that this was going to be a work of journalism, that it was going to be written by me,
sentences.zh: 我从一开始就向道恩明确了我的意图，即这将是一篇新闻报道，由我撰写，

sentences.en: and that, of course, Sonia Larson would be thoroughly quoted in the story, too.
sentences.zh: 当然，索尼娅·拉尔森也会在报道中被充分引用。

sentences.en: And she was fine with that.
sentences.zh: 她对此表示同意。

sentences.en: So about the title of the story, who is the bad art friend?
sentences.zh: 关于这个故事的标题《谁是糟糕的艺术朋友》，

sentences.en: I just have to say I didn't set out to write a whodunit or to point fingers at one person or another.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我并不是为了写一个“谁干的”侦探故事，也不是为了指责某个人。

sentences.en: I think the story overall does its best to capture two complicated people who end up on a collision course with one another.
sentences.zh: 我认为整个故事尽力捕捉了两个复杂的人，她们最终走向了彼此碰撞的轨道。

sentences.en: And maybe the recent Twitter conversation and the online reaction to the article has kind of flattened the portraits in the story into good guys versus bad guys.
sentences.zh: 也许最近推特上的讨论和网络对这篇文章的反应，已经把故事中人物的形象简化成了“好人”与“坏人”的对立。

sentences.en: But what the Twitter debate shows is that any moment we can go into our own echo chambers and decide that one person is right and the other is wrong,
sentences.zh: 但推特上的争论恰恰表明，我们随时都可能陷入自己的回声室，认定一个人是对的，另一个人是错的，

sentences.en: which can turn any of us into bad art friends.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让我们任何人都变成“糟糕的艺术朋友”。

sentences.en: So here's my story from the New York Times Magazine, who is the bad art friend, read by Samantha Dez.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为《纽约时报杂志》撰写的故事《谁是糟糕的艺术朋友》，由萨曼莎·德兹朗读。

sentences.en: This was recorded by Autumn.
sentences.zh: 这是由Autumn录制的。

sentences.en: Autumn is an app you can download to listen to lots of audio stories from publications such as The New York Times,
sentences.zh: Autumn是一款你可以下载的应用程序，用来收听来自《纽约时报》等出版物的许多音频故事，

sentences.en: The New Yorker, Vanity Fair, and The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 还有《纽约客》、《名利场》和《大西洋月刊》。

sentences.en: There is a sunny earnestness to Dawn Dorland, an unselfconscious openness that endears her to some people and that others have found to be a little extra.
sentences.zh: 道恩·多兰身上有一种阳光般的真诚，一种不加掩饰的坦率，这让她在一些人眼中很可爱，但也有人觉得她有点“戏多”。

sentences.en: Her friends call her a feeler, open-hearted and eager, pressing to make connections with others, even as, in many instances, she feels like an outsider.
sentences.zh: 她的朋友称她为“感性的人”，心胸开阔且热切，努力与他人建立联系，尽管在许多情况下，她觉得自己像个局外人。

sentences.en: An essayist and aspiring novelist who has taught writing classes in Los Angeles, she is the sort of writer who, in one authorial mission statement,
sentences.zh: 作为一名散文家和有抱负的小说家，她曾在洛杉矶教过写作课，她是那种在某份创作宣言中，

sentences.en: declares her faith in the power of fiction to share truth, to heal trauma, to build bridges.
sentences.zh: 宣称自己相信小说分享真相、治愈创伤、架起桥梁的力量的作家。

sentences.en: I'm compelled at funerals to shake hands with the dusty men who dig our graves, she has written.
sentences.zh: “在葬礼上，我忍不住想去和那些挖掘我们坟墓的尘土飞扬的人握手，”她曾这样写道。

sentences.en: She is known for signing off her emails, not with all best or sincerely, but kindly.
sentences.zh: 她以在邮件结尾不写“祝好”或“诚挚地”，而是写“善意地”而闻名。

sentences.en: On June 24, 2015, a year after completing her MFA in creative writing,
sentences.zh: 2015年6月24日，在她获得创意写作艺术硕士学位一年后，

sentences.en: Dorland did perhaps the kindest, most consequential thing she might ever do in her life.
sentences.zh: 多兰做了她一生中可能做过的最善良、影响最深远的事情。

sentences.en: She donated one of her kidneys, and elected to do it in a slightly unusual and particularly altruistic way.
sentences.zh: 她捐献了自己的一颗肾脏，并选择了一种略显不同寻常且特别无私的方式。

sentences.en: As a so-called non-directed donation, her kidney was not meant for anyone in particular,
sentences.zh: 作为所谓的“非定向捐赠”，她的肾脏并非指定给某个人，

sentences.en: but instead was part of a donation chain, coordinated by surgeons to provide a kidney to a recipient who may otherwise have no other living donor.
sentences.zh: 而是参与了一个捐赠链，由外科医生协调，为那些可能没有其他活体捐赠者的受赠者提供肾脏。

sentences.en: There was some risk with the procedure, of course, and a recovery to think about, and a one-kidney life to lead from that point forward.
sentences.zh: 当然，手术本身存在一定风险，还要考虑术后恢复，以及此后只剩一颗肾脏的生活。

sentences.en: But in truth, Dorland, in her 30s at the time, had been wanting to do it for years.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，当时30多岁的多兰多年来一直想这么做。

sentences.en: As soon as I learned I could, she told me recently, on the phone from her home in Los Angeles, where she and her husband were caring for their toddler son and elderly pit bull,
sentences.zh: “我一知道自己可以这样做，”她最近在洛杉矶的家中通过电话告诉我，当时她和丈夫正在照顾他们蹒跚学步的儿子和年迈的比特犬，

sentences.en: and, in their spare time, volunteering at dog shelters and searching for adoptive families for feral cat litters.
sentences.zh: 闲暇时，他们还会去动物收容所做志愿者，并为野猫窝寻找领养家庭。

sentences.en: It's kind of like not overthinking love, you know?
sentences.zh: “这就像不去过度思考爱，你懂吗？”

sentences.en: Several weeks before the surgery, Dorland decided to share her truth with others.
sentences.zh: 手术前几周，多兰决定与他人分享她的真相。

sentences.en: She started a private Facebook group, inviting family and friends, including some fellow writers from Grub Street,
sentences.zh: 她建立了一个私密的Facebook群组，邀请了家人和朋友，包括一些来自“Grub Street”的同行作家，

sentences.en: the Boston Writing Center where Dorland had spent many years learning her craft.
sentences.zh: 那是波士顿写作中心，多兰在那里花了很多年学习她的手艺。

sentences.en: After her surgery, she posted something to her group, a heartfelt letter she'd written to the final recipient of the surgical chain, whoever they may be.
sentences.zh: 手术后，她在群组里发布了一条消息，那是一封她写给手术链最终受赠者的感人信件，无论那个人是谁。

sentences.en: Personally, my childhood was marked by trauma and abuse.
sentences.zh: “个人而言，我的童年充满了创伤和虐待。”

sentences.en: I didn't have the opportunity to form secure attachments with my family of origin.
sentences.zh: “我没有机会与原生家庭建立安全依恋。”

sentences.en: A positive outcome of my early life is empathy, that it opened a well of possibility between me and strangers.
sentences.zh: “我早年生活的一个积极结果是同理心，它在我与陌生人之间开启了一口可能性的深井。”

sentences.en: While perhaps many more people would be motivated to donate an organ to a friend or family member in need, To me, the suffering of strangers is just as real.
sentences.zh: “虽然也许更多人会有动力向需要帮助的朋友或家人捐赠器官，但对我来说，陌生人的痛苦同样真实。”

sentences.en: Throughout my preparation for becoming a donor, I focused a majority of my mental energy on imagining and celebrating you.
sentences.zh: “在为成为捐赠者做准备的过程中，我将大部分精神力量都集中在想象和赞美你身上。”

sentences.en: The procedure went well.
sentences.zh: 手术很成功。

sentences.en: By a stroke of luck, Dorland would even get to meet the recipient, an Orthodox Jewish man, and take photos with him and his family.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，多兰甚至见到了受赠者，一位正统犹太教男子，并与他和他的家人合了影。

sentences.en: In time, Dorland would start posting outside the private group to all of Facebook, celebrating her one-year kidneyversary,
sentences.zh: 后来，多兰开始在私密群组之外向整个Facebook发布消息，庆祝她捐肾一周年，

sentences.en: and appearing as a UCLA Health Laker for a day at the Staples Center to support live organ donation.
sentences.zh: 并以“加州大学洛杉矶分校健康中心湖人队一日成员”的身份出现在斯台普斯中心，支持活体器官捐赠。

sentences.en: But just after the surgery, when she checked Facebook,
sentences.zh: 但就在手术后，当她查看Facebook时，

sentences.en: Dorland noticed some people she'd invited into the group hadn't seemed to react to any of her posts.
sentences.zh: 多兰注意到一些她邀请进群的人似乎对她的任何帖子都没有反应。

sentences.en: On July 20th, she wrote an email to one of them.
sentences.zh: 7月20日，她给其中一个人发了一封邮件。

sentences.en: A writer named Sonia Larson.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫索尼娅·拉尔森的作家。

sentences.en: Larson and Dorland had met eight years earlier in Boston.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森和多兰八年前在波士顿相识。

sentences.en: They were just a few years apart in age, and for several years they ran in the same circles, hitting the same events, readings, and workshops at the Grub Street Writing Center.
sentences.zh: 她们年龄相差不大，有几年她们在同一个圈子里活动，参加同样的活动、朗诵会和Grub Street写作中心的研讨会。

sentences.en: But in the years since Dorland left town, Larson had leveled up.
sentences.zh: 但在多兰离开后的几年里，拉尔森的水平提升了。

sentences.en: Her short fiction was published in Best American Short Stories and elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 她的短篇小说发表在《美国最佳短篇小说》等刊物上。

sentences.en: She took charge of Grub Street's annual Muse and the Marketplace Literary Conference.
sentences.zh: 她负责了Grub Street年度“缪斯与市场”文学会议。

sentences.en: And as a mixed-race Asian American, she marshaled the group's diversity efforts.
sentences.zh: 作为一名亚裔混血美国人，她还负责了该组织的多元化工作。

sentences.en: She also joined a group of published writers that calls itself the Chunky Monkeys,
sentences.zh: 她还加入了一个自称为“胖猴子”的已出版作家小组，

sentences.en: a whimsical name referring to breaking off little chunks of big projects to share with the other members.
sentences.zh: 这是一个异想天开的名字，指的是把大项目拆分成小块分享给其他成员。

sentences.en: One of those writing group members, Celeste Ng, who wrote Little Fires Everywhere, told me that she admires Larson's ability to create characters who have these big blind spots.
sentences.zh: 该写作小组的成员之一，写过《小小火苗》的塞莱斯特·吴告诉我，她很钦佩拉尔森创造那些有巨大盲点的人物角色的能力。

sentences.en: While they think they're presenting themselves one way, they actually come across as something else entirely.
sentences.zh: 当她们以为自己是以某种方式展示自己时，实际上给人的印象却完全不同。

sentences.en: When it comes to literary success, the stakes can be pretty low.
sentences.zh: 在文学成就方面，赌注可能相当低。

sentences.en: A fellowship, a residency here, a short story published there.
sentences.zh: 一个奖学金，一个驻留机会，一篇发表的短篇小说。

sentences.en: But it seemed as if Larson was having the sort of writing life that Dorland once dreamed of having.
sentences.zh: 但看起来拉尔森过着多兰曾经梦想的那种写作生活。

sentences.en: After many years, Dorland, still teaching, had yet to be published.
sentences.zh: 多年过去了，多兰还在教书，却尚未发表作品。

sentences.en: But to an extent that she once had a writing community, Grub Street was it.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，如果她曾经拥有过一个写作社区，那就是Grub Street。

sentences.en: And Larson was, she believed, a close friend.
sentences.zh: 而拉尔森，她曾认为是亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: Over email on July 21st, 2015, Larson answered Dorland's message with a chirpy reply.
sentences.zh: 2015年7月21日，拉尔森通过电子邮件回复了多兰的消息，语气轻快。

sentences.en: How have you been, my dear?
sentences.zh: “亲爱的，你最近怎么样？”

sentences.en: Dorland replied with a rundown of her next writing residencies and workshops.
sentences.zh: 多兰回复了一份她接下来的写作驻留和研讨会的清单。

sentences.en: And as casually as possible, asked, I think you're aware that I donated my kidney this summer, right?
sentences.zh: 并尽可能随意地问道：“我想你知道我今年夏天捐了肾，对吧？”

sentences.en: Only then did Larson gush.
sentences.zh: 直到那时，拉尔森才表现出热情。

sentences.en: Ah, yes, I did see on Facebook that you donated your kidney.
sentences.zh: “啊，是的，我在Facebook上看到你捐了肾。”

sentences.en: What a tremendous thing.
sentences.zh: “真是了不起的事情。”

sentences.en: Afterward, Dorland would wonder, if she really thought it was that great, why did she need reminding that it happened?
sentences.zh: 事后，多兰不禁怀疑，如果她真的觉得这事儿那么棒，为什么还需要提醒她才想起来？

sentences.en: They wouldn't cross paths again until the following spring.
sentences.zh: 直到次年春天，她们才再次交集。

sentences.en: A brief hello at AWP, the annual writing conference, where the subject of Dorland's kidney went unmentioned.
sentences.zh: 在年度写作会议AWP上简单地打了个招呼，多兰捐肾的话题只字未提。

sentences.en: A month later, at the Grub Street Muse conference in Boston,
sentences.zh: 一个月后，在波士顿的Grub Street缪斯会议上，

sentences.en: Dorland sensed something had shifted.
sentences.zh: 多兰感觉到有些事情发生了变化。

sentences.en: Not just with Larson, but with various Grub Street eminences.
sentences.zh: 不仅是拉尔森，还有Grub Street的各种名流。

sentences.en: Old friends and mentors of hers who also happened to be members of Larson's writing group, the Chunky Monkeys.
sentences.zh: 她的一些老朋友和导师，恰好也是拉尔森写作小组“胖猴子”的成员。

sentences.en: Barely anyone brought up what she'd done, even though everyone must have known she'd done it.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有人提起她做过的事，尽管每个人肯定都知道她做了这件事。

sentences.en: It was a little bit like if you've been at a funeral and nobody wanted to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 这有点像如果你参加了一场葬礼，却没人想谈论它一样。

sentences.en: It just was strange to me, she said.
sentences.zh: “这对我来说很奇怪，”她说。

sentences.en: I left that conference with this question.
sentences.zh: 我带着这个问题离开了那个会议。

sentences.en: Do writers not care about my kidney donation?
sentences.zh: 作家们不关心我的肾脏捐赠吗？

sentences.en: Which kind of confused me because I thought I was in a community of service-oriented people.
sentences.zh: 这让我有点困惑，因为我以为我身处一个服务导向的群体中。

sentences.en: It didn't take long for a clue to surface.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，线索就浮出水面了。

sentences.en: On June 24th, 2016, a Facebook friend of Dorland's named Tom Meek commented on one of Dorland's posts.
sentences.zh: 2016年6月24日，多兰的一位Facebook好友汤姆·米克评论了多兰的一篇帖子。

sentences.en: Sonia read a cool story about giving out a kidney.
sentences.zh: “索尼娅读了一个关于捐肾的酷故事。”

sentences.en: You came to mind, and I wondered if you were the source of inspiration?
sentences.zh: “我想到了你，不知道你是不是灵感来源？”

sentences.en: Still impressed you did this.
sentences.zh: “依然为你做过这件事感到钦佩。”

sentences.en: Dorland was confused.
sentences.zh: 多兰很困惑。

sentences.en: A year earlier, Larson could hardly be bothered to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 一年前，拉尔森几乎懒得谈论这件事。

sentences.en: Now, at Trident Bookstore in Boston, she'd apparently read from a new short story about that very subject.
sentences.zh: 现在，在波士顿的Trident书店，她显然朗读了一篇关于这个主题的新短篇小说。

sentences.en: Meek had tagged Larson in his comments, so Dorland thought that Larson must have seen it.
sentences.zh: 米克在评论中标记了拉尔森，所以多兰认为拉尔森一定看到了。

sentences.en: She waited for Larson to chime in, to say,
sentences.zh: 她等着拉尔森插话，说，

sentences.en: Oh, yes, I'd meant to tell you, Dawn, or something like that.
sentences.zh: “哦，是的，我本来想告诉你的，道恩，”或者类似的话。

sentences.en: But there was nothing.
sentences.zh: 但什么都没有。

sentences.en: Why would Sonia write about it, she wondered, and not tell her?
sentences.zh: 她纳闷，为什么索尼娅要写这个，却不告诉她？

sentences.en: Six days later, she decided to ask her.
sentences.zh: 六天后，她决定去问她。

sentences.en: Much as she had a year earlier, she sent Larson a friendly email, including one pointed requeSt.
sentences.zh: 就像一年前一样，她给拉尔森发了一封友好的邮件，其中包含了一个明确的请求。

sentences.en: Hey, I heard you wrote a kidney donation story.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我听说你写了一个关于肾脏捐赠的故事。

sentences.en: Cool, can I read it?
sentences.zh: 很酷，我可以读读吗？

sentences.en: Ten days later, Larson wrote back saying that, yes, she was working on a story about a woman who receives a kidney, partially inspired by how my imagination took off
sentences.zh: 十天后，拉尔森回信说，是的，她正在写一个关于接受肾脏的女性的故事，部分灵感来自于我的想象力在

sentences.en: after learning of your own tremendous donation.
sentences.zh: 得知你那伟大的捐赠后被激发了。

sentences.en: In her writing, she spun out a scenario based not on Dorland, she said, but on something else, themes that have always fascinated her.
sentences.zh: 她说，在她的写作中，她构思的情节并非基于多兰，而是基于其他东西，那些一直让她着迷的主题。

sentences.en: I hope it doesn't feel too weird for your gift to have inspired works of art,
sentences.zh: “希望你的善举激发了艺术作品不会让你觉得太奇怪，”

sentences.en: Larson wrote.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森写道。

sentences.en: Dorland wrote back within hours.
sentences.zh: 多兰在几小时内就回了信。

sentences.en: She admitted to being a little surprised, especially since we're friends and you hadn't mentioned it.
sentences.zh: 她承认感到有点惊讶，特别是“因为我们是朋友，而你之前没提过”。

sentences.en: The next day, Larson replied, her tone a bit removed, stressing that her story was, not about you or your particular gift, but about narrative possibilities I began thinking about.
sentences.zh: 第二天，拉尔森回复了，语气有点疏离，强调她的故事“不是关于你或你的特定善举，而是关于我开始思考的叙事可能性”。

sentences.en: But Dorland pressed on.
sentences.zh: 但多兰继续追问。

sentences.en: It's the interpersonal layer that feels off to me, Sonia.
sentences.zh: “索尼娅，人际层面的东西让我觉得不对劲。”

sentences.en: You seemed not to be aware of my donation until I pointed it out.
sentences.zh: “在我指出之前，你似乎并不知道我的捐赠。”

sentences.en: But if you had already kicked off your fictional project at this time, well, I think your behavior is a little deceptive, at least weird.
sentences.zh: “但如果你当时已经开始了你的虚构项目，嗯，我觉得你的行为有点欺骗性，至少很奇怪。”

sentences.en: Larson's answer this time was even cooler.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森这次的回答更加冷淡。

sentences.en: Before this email exchange, she wrote,
sentences.zh: 她写道，在这次邮件交流之前，

sentences.en: I hadn't considered that my individual vocal support, or absence of it, was of much significance.
sentences.zh: “我没考虑过我个人的口头支持，或者缺乏支持，有什么重大意义。”

sentences.en: Which, though it was shrouded in politesse, was a different point altogether.
sentences.zh: 虽然这番话包裹在礼貌之中，但完全是另一个重点。

sentences.en: Who, Larson seemed to be saying, said we were such good friends?
sentences.zh: 拉尔森似乎在说：谁说我们是那么好的朋友？

sentences.en: For many years now,
sentences.zh: 多年来，

sentences.en: Dorland has been working on a sprawling novel,
sentences.zh: 多兰一直在创作一部宏大的小说，

sentences.en: Econoline, which interweaves a knowing present-day perspective with vivid, sometimes brutal, but often romantic remembrances of an itinerant rural childhood.
sentences.zh: 《Econoline》，它将一种清醒的当代视角与对流浪乡村童年的生动、有时残酷但往往浪漫的回忆交织在一起。

sentences.en: The van in the title is, she writes in a recent draft, blue as a tidy bowl tablet, bumbling on the highway, bulky and off kilter, a June bug in the wind.
sentences.zh: 她在最近的草稿中写道，标题中的那辆面包车“像一片Tidy Bowl清洁片一样蓝，在高速公路上笨拙地行驶，庞大而倾斜，像风中的六月甲虫”。

sentences.en: The family in the narrative survives on government flour, canned juice, and beans, and rule-along bricks of lard that the father calls commodities.
sentences.zh: 叙事中的家庭靠政府发放的面粉、罐装果汁、豆子以及父亲称之为“商品”的规则砖块状猪油维持生活。

sentences.en: Dorland is not shy about explaining how her past has afforded her a degree of moral clarity that others might not come by so easily.
sentences.zh: 多兰并不避讳解释她的过去如何赋予了她一种别人可能不容易获得的道德清晰度。

sentences.en: She was raised in near poverty in rural Iowa.
sentences.zh: 她在爱荷华州农村的贫困环境中长大。

sentences.en: Her parents moved around a lot, she told me, and the whole family lived under a stigma.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她的父母经常搬家，全家人都生活在一种耻辱感中。

sentences.en: One small consolation was the way her mother modeled a certain perverse self-reliance, rejecting the judgments of others.
sentences.zh: 一个小小的安慰是她母亲表现出的一种反常的自力更生方式，拒绝他人的评判。

sentences.en: Another is how her turbulent youth has served as a wellspring for much of her writing.
sentences.zh: 另一个安慰是她动荡的青春如何成为她大部分写作的源泉。

sentences.en: She made her way out of Iowa with a scholarship to Scripps College in California, followed by Divinity School at Harvard.
sentences.zh: 她凭借加州斯克里普斯学院的奖学金走出了爱荷华州，随后进入哈佛神学院深造。

sentences.en: Unsure of what to do next, she worked day jobs in advertising in Boston while dabbling in workshops at the Grub Street Writing Center.
sentences.zh: 由于不知道下一步该做什么，她在波士顿做着广告业的零工，同时在格鲁布街写作中心（Grub Street Writing Center）参加一些研讨会。

sentences.en: When she noticed classmates cooing over Marilyn Robinson's novel Housekeeping, she picked up a copy.
sentences.zh: 当她注意到同学们对玛丽莲·罗宾逊的小说《管家》（Housekeeping）赞不绝口时，她也买了一本。

sentences.en: After inhaling its story of an eccentric small-town upbringing told with sensitive, all-seeing narration,
sentences.zh: 在沉浸于书中那个以细腻、全知视角讲述的古怪小镇成长故事后，

sentences.en: she knew she wanted to become a writer.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己想成为一名作家。

sentences.en: At Grub Street,
sentences.zh: 在格鲁布街，

sentences.en: Dorland eventually became one of several teaching scholars at the Muse Conference, leading workshops on such topics as truth and taboo, writing past shame.
sentences.zh: 多兰最终成为了缪斯大会（Muse Conference）的几位教学学者之一，主持关于真相与禁忌、克服羞耻感写作等主题的研讨会。

sentences.en: Dorland credits two members of the Chunky Monkeys group,
sentences.zh: 多兰将自己的成功归功于“胖猴子”（Chunky Monkeys）小组的两名成员，

sentences.en: Adam Stumacher and Chris Castellani, with advising her.
sentences.zh: 亚当·斯图马赫（Adam Stumacher）和克里斯·卡斯特拉尼（Chris Castellani），感谢他们的建议。

sentences.en: But in hindsight, much of her Grub Street experience is tied up with her memories of Sonia Larson.
sentences.zh: 但事后看来，她在格鲁布街的大部分经历都与她对索尼娅·拉尔森（Sonia Larson）的记忆交织在一起。

sentences.en: She thinks they first met at a one-off writing workshop
sentences.zh: 她认为她们第一次见面是在一次写作研讨会上，

sentences.en: Larson taught, though Larson, for her part, says she doesn't remember this.
sentences.zh: 那是拉尔森教的，尽管拉尔森本人说她不记得这件事了。

sentences.en: Everybody at Grub Street knew Larson.
sentences.zh: 格鲁布街的每个人都认识拉尔森。

sentences.en: She was one of the popular, ever-present people who worked there.
sentences.zh: 她是那里受欢迎且无处不在的人之一。

sentences.en: On nights out with other Grubbies,
sentences.zh: 在与其他“格鲁布人”外出聚会的夜晚，

sentences.en: Dorland remembers Larson getting personal, confiding about an engagement, the death of someone she knew, and plans to apply to MFA prograMs.
sentences.zh: 多兰记得拉尔森会谈论私事，倾诉关于订婚、熟人去世以及申请艺术硕士（MFA）项目的计划。

sentences.en: Though Larson now says she shared such things widely.
sentences.zh: 尽管拉尔森现在说她当时向很多人分享过这些事情。

sentences.en: When a job at Grub Street opened up,
sentences.zh: 当格鲁布街有一个职位空缺时，

sentences.en: Larson encouraged her to apply.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森鼓励她去申请。

sentences.en: Even when she didn't get it, everyone was so gracious about it, including Larson, that she felt included all the same.
sentences.zh: 即使她没得到那份工作，每个人——包括拉尔森——都表现得非常大度，让她依然感到自己是其中的一员。

sentences.en: Now, as she read these strained emails from Larson about this story of a kidney donation, her kidney donation,
sentences.zh: 现在，当她读到拉尔森发来的这些关于肾脏捐赠故事（她的肾脏捐赠）的紧张邮件时，

sentences.en: Dorland wondered if everyone at Grub Street had been playing a different game, with rules she'd failed to grasp.
sentences.zh: 多兰不禁怀疑，格鲁布街的每个人是否一直在玩一场她没能理解规则的游戏。

sentences.en: On July 15, 2016,
Dorland's tone turned brittle, even wounded.
sentences.zh: 多兰的语气变得生硬，甚至受伤。

sentences.en: Here was a friend entrusting something to you, making herself vulnerable to you.
sentences.zh: 这是一个朋友在向你托付心事，向你敞开心扉。

sentences.en: At least the conclusion I can draw from your responses is that I was mistaken to consider us the friends that I did.
sentences.zh: 至少从你的回复中我得出的结论是，我错把我们当成了真正的朋友。

sentences.en: Larson didn't answer right away.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森没有立即回复。

sentences.en: Three days later,
sentences.zh: 三天后，

sentences.en: Dorland took her frustrations to Facebook in a blind item.
sentences.zh: 多兰在Facebook上发布了一条不点名的动态，表达了她的沮丧。

sentences.en: I discovered that a writer friend has based a short story on something momentous I did in my own life, without telling me or ever intending to tell me.
sentences.zh: 我发现一位作家朋友以我生活中发生的一件重大事件为基础写了一篇短篇小说，却从未告诉我，也从未打算告诉我。

sentences.en: Another writer tipped me off.
sentences.zh: 是另一位作家提醒我的。

sentences.en: Still nothing from Larson.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森依然没有回应。

sentences.en: Dorland waited another day and then sent her another message, both in a text and in an email.
sentences.zh: 多兰又等了一天，然后又发了一条信息，通过短信和电子邮件同时发送。

sentences.en: I'm still surprised that you didn't care about my personal feelings.
sentences.zh: 我仍然很惊讶你竟然不在乎我的个人感受。

sentences.en: I wish you'd given me the benefit of the doubt that I wouldn't interfere.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能相信我不会去干涉。

sentences.en: Yet again, no response.
sentences.zh: 依然没有回应。

sentences.en: The next day, on July 20, she wrote again.
sentences.zh: 第二天，7月20日，她又写道。

sentences.en: Am I correct that you do not want to make peace?
sentences.zh: 我理解得对吗，你不想和解？

sentences.en: Not hearing from you sends that message.
sentences.zh: 你不回复就传达了这个信息。

sentences.en: Larson answered this time.
sentences.zh: 这一次拉尔森回复了。

sentences.en: I see that you're merely expressing real hurt, and for that, I am truly sorry.
sentences.zh: 我看得出你只是在表达真实的伤害，对此我深表歉意。

sentences.en: She wrote on July 21St.
sentences.zh: 她在7月21日写道。

sentences.en: But she also changed gears a little.
sentences.zh: 但她也稍微改变了态度。

sentences.en: I myself have seen references to my own life in others' fiction, and it certainly felt weird at firSt.
sentences.zh: 我自己也曾在别人的小说中看到过关于我生活的影子，起初确实感觉很奇怪。

sentences.en: But I maintain that they have a right to write about what they want, as do I, and as do you.
sentences.zh: 但我坚持认为他们有权写他们想写的东西，正如我有权，你也有权。

sentences.en: Hurt feelings or not,
sentences.zh: 无论是否感到受伤，

sentences.en: Larson was articulating an ideal, a principle she felt she and all writers ought to live up to.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森都在阐述一种理想，一种她认为她和所有作家都应该践行的原则。

sentences.en: For me, honoring another's artistic freedom is a gesture of friendship,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，尊重他人的艺术自由是一种友谊的姿态，

sentences.en: Larson wrote, and of truSt.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森写道，也是一种信任。

sentences.en: Like Dawn Dorland,
sentences.zh: 像道恩·多兰（Dawn Dorland）一样，

sentences.en: Sonia Larson understands life as an outsider.
sentences.zh: 索尼娅·拉尔森（Sonia Larson）以局外人的视角理解生活。

sentences.en: The daughter of a
sentences.zh: 作为一位

sentences.en: Chinese-American mother and white father, she was brought up in a predominantly white middle-class enclave in Minnesota, where being mixed race sometimes confused her.
sentences.zh: 华裔母亲和白人父亲的女儿，她在明尼苏达州一个以白人为主的中产阶级聚居区长大，在那里，混血身份有时会让她感到困惑。

sentences.en: It took me a while to realize the things I was teased about were intertwined with my race, she told me over the phone from Somerville, where she lived with her husband
sentences.zh: 我花了一段时间才意识到，我被嘲笑的事情与我的种族有关，她在萨默维尔（Somerville）通过电话告诉我，她和丈夫以及女儿住在那儿。

sentences.en: and baby daughter.
sentences.zh: 在2017年版《美国最佳短篇小说》中入选的短篇小说《盖比·多夫》（Gabe Dove）中，

sentences.en: Her dark hair, her slight build, in a short story called Gabe Dove, which was picked for the 2017 edition of Best American Short Stories,
sentences.zh: 她那深色的头发、瘦小的身躯，

sentences.en: Larson's protagonist is a second-generation
sentences.zh: 拉尔森的主角是一位第二代

sentences.en: Asian-American woman named Shen Tao, who is used to men putting their fingers around her wrist and remarking on how narrow they are, almost as if she were a toy, a doll,
sentences.zh: 亚裔美国女性，名叫沈涛（Shen Tao），她习惯了男人们用手指环绕她的手腕，评论她的手腕有多细，仿佛她是一个玩具、一个玩偶，

sentences.en: a plaything.
sentences.zh: 一个玩物。

sentences.en: Larson's path toward writing was more conventional than Dorland's.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森的写作之路比多兰更传统。

sentences.en: She started earlier, after her first creative writing class at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
sentences.zh: 她在威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校上了第一堂创意写作课后，就开始得更早了。

sentences.en: When she graduated in 2005, she moved to Boston and walked into Grub Street to volunteer the next day.
sentences.zh: 2005年毕业后，她搬到波士顿，第二天就走进格鲁布街做志愿者。

sentences.en: Right away, she became one of a handful of people who kept the place running.
sentences.zh: 她很快就成为了维持该机构运作的少数核心人员之一。

sentences.en: In her fiction,
sentences.zh: 在小说创作中，

sentences.en: Larson began exploring the sensitive subject matter that had always fascinated her, racial dynamics, and people caught between cultures.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森开始探索那些一直让她着迷的敏感题材：种族动态，以及夹在不同文化之间的人们。

sentences.en: In time, she moved beyond mere political commentary to revel in her character's flaws, like a more socially responsible Philip Roth, though every bit as happy to be profane and fun
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，她超越了单纯的政治评论，开始沉醉于塑造角色的缺陷，就像一个更具社会责任感的菲利普·罗斯（Philip Roth），尽管她同样乐于表现得粗俗、有趣

sentences.en: and provocative.
sentences.zh: 且具有挑衅性。

sentences.en: Even as she allows readers to be one step ahead of her characters, to see how they're going astray, her writing luxuriates in the seductive power that comes from living
sentences.zh: 即使她让读者比角色领先一步，看到他们如何误入歧途，她的文字依然沉溺于那种生活在

sentences.en: an unmoored life.
sentences.zh: 漂泊状态中所带来的诱人力量。

sentences.en: He described thick winding streams and lush mountain gorges.
sentences.zh: 他描述了蜿蜒的溪流和郁郁葱葱的山谷。

sentences.en: The rudderless
sentences.zh: 在《盖比·多夫》中，

sentences.en: Shun Tao narrates in Gabe Dove, obviously thinking
sentences.zh: 漫无目的的沈涛叙述道，显然认为

sentences.en: I'd enjoy this window into my ancestral country.
sentences.zh: 我会喜欢这种了解我祖籍国的窗口。

sentences.en: But in truth, I wanted to slap him.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我想扇他一巴掌。

sentences.en: Shun Tao, or a character with that name, turns up in many of Larson's stories as a sort of a motif, a little different each time
sentences.zh: 沈涛，或者叫这个名字的角色，出现在拉尔森的许多故事中，作为一种母题，每次都有所不同，

sentences.en: Larson deploys her.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森运用着她。

sentences.en: She appears again in The Kindest, the story that Larson had been reading from at the Trident Bookstore in 2016.
sentences.zh: 她再次出现在《最善良的人》（The Kindest）中，这是拉尔森2016年在三叉戟书店（Trident Bookstore）朗读的故事。

sentences.en: Here,
sentences.zh: 在这里，

sentences.en: Shun Tao is married with an alcohol problem.
sentences.zh: 沈涛已婚并有酗酒问题。

sentences.en: A car crash precipitates the need for a new organ, and her whole family is hoping the donation will serve as a wake-up call, a chance for Shun Tao to redeem herself.
sentences.zh: 一场车祸引发了对新器官的需求，她的全家人都希望这次捐赠能成为一个警钟，让沈涛有机会自我救赎。

sentences.en: That's when the donor materializes.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，捐赠者出现了。

sentences.en: White, wealthy, and entitled, the woman who gave
sentences.zh: 白人、富有且自以为是，那个给

sentences.en: Shun Tao her kidney is not exactly an uncomplicated altruiSt.
sentences.zh: 沈涛捐肾的女人并非一个单纯的利他主义者。

sentences.en: She is a stranger to her own impulses, unaware of how what she considers a selfless act also contains elements of intense, unbridled narcissism.
sentences.zh: 她对自己内心的冲动感到陌生，没有意识到她所认为的无私行为中，也包含了强烈、肆无忌惮的自恋成分。

sentences.en: In early drafts of the story, the donor character's name was Dawn.
sentences.zh: 在故事的初稿中，捐赠者的名字叫道恩（Dawn）。

sentences.en: In later drafts,
sentences.zh: 在后来的草稿中，

sentences.en: Larson ended up changing the name to Rose.
sentences.zh: 拉尔森最终把名字改成了罗斯（Rose）。

sentences.en: While Dorland, no doubt, was an inspiration,
sentences.zh: 虽然多兰无疑是一个灵感来源，

sentences.en: Larson argues that in its finished form, her story moved far beyond anything Dorland herself had ever said or done.
sentences.zh: 但拉尔森认为，在最终成稿中，她的故事已经远远超出了多兰本人所说或所做的任何事情。

sentences.en: But in every iteration of The Kindest, the donor says she wants to meet Shun Tao to celebrate, to commune.
